Intermediate.learningGoal: Write reusable generic types and methods with the right constraints.
gotchas: Using object and casts where a type parameter would keep type safety
Missing constraint (where T : IComparable<T>) forces runtime checks
default(T) is null for reference types and zero for value types
goodSolutionShows: Constraints that express exactly what the code needs
No boxing or casting inside the generic code
Generic methods with type inference at the call site
shapeHints: a bounded cache keyed by T

Advanced.learningGoal: Use variance, static abstract interface members and generic math to build flexible APIs.
gotchas: in/out variance only works on interfaces and delegates, not classes
Covariant IEnumerable<Derived> to IEnumerable<Base> but not List<Derived> to List<Base>
Generic math needs INumber<T> style constraints, not dynamic
goodSolutionShows: Static abstract members or INumber<T> for arithmetic on T
APIs that are easy to call without explicit type arguments
shapeHints: a generic Sum/Average over any INumber<T>
a read-only repository interface with covariance

Expert.learningGoal: Reason about generic specialisation, struct constraints and allocation-free generic code.
gotchas: Interface constraints on structs avoid boxing only when called through the type parameter
Shared generic code for reference types vs specialised code for value types
goodSolutionShows: Static abstract interface members used deliberately
shapeHints: a typed ID<TEntity> with parsing via static abstract members
